problem: An indented Quick button under the global Configuration disclosure invents a third navigation depth and makes a local content choice look like an application destination.
scope: configuration disclosure, explorer resource/quick switching, hierarchy geometry, keyboard semantics, persistence, and compact browser layouts
baseline: The global left rail contains Configuration followed by a smaller indented Quick button; both use the same navigation treatment despite owning different levels.
benchmarks: VS Code Activity Bar items own top-level View Containers
Fluent 2 Tablist for a small set of closely related frequently accessed categories
WAI-ARIA tablist, tab, tabpanel, selected state and roving focus
advantages: The existing configuration disclosure and persisted source-view state remain usable
Both local panels are already immediate and need no asynchronous preload
Native React buttons avoid a new runtime dependency
disadvantages: The current rail gives a local choice the same visual owner as application destinations
Indentation is unexplained and changes at compact widths
The old pressed-button state does not expose peer-view keyboard conventions
limitations: Horizontal tabs are appropriate only while the choice count remains small
The resource action toolbar must retain enough width beside the tabs
Legacy Chrome and Firefox prevent relying on container queries or new CSS primitives
bottlenecks: visual ownership must be checked in a real browser rather than inferred from DOM presence
switching must not unmount the editor or lose drafts and run inputs
resource actions and two labels must fit the fixed explorer width

metrics.name: global rail local-view controls
metrics.measurement: source contract plus browser role/geometry assertions

metrics.name: selected local tabs
metrics.measurement: aria-selected count in the owning explorer header

metrics.name: keyboard switching coverage
metrics.measurement: Playwright keyboard activation and selected-panel assertions

hypotheses: Moving local selection into the explorer header removes the false third level without hiding either option
A quiet underline tablist communicates peer views more clearly than nested rail buttons
Automatic activation is appropriate because both panels switch immediately
allowed_variables: resource and quick view control semantics

stages.output: a gate that rejects a local switch under the global rail
explorer-header peer tablist and associated panels
stages.checker: build, role assertions and keyboard flow

stages.output: wide, focused and compact screenshots plus accessibility receipt
stages.rollback: earliest failed structure or styling owner

hard_gates: exactly one resource/quick tab is selected
collapse makes the local tablist unavailable while preserving state
drafts, selected file and run inputs survive switching
wide and compact layouts have no overflow or clipped resource actions
failure_fixtures: resource and quick are styled as nested global navigation buttons
both tabs are tabbable or selected
arrow keys do not change the active panel
success_fixtures: global rail contains one Configuration disclosure only
explorer header contains Resource and Quick peer tabs
one underline marks selection without nested indentation
keyboard switching preserves the workbench context
rollback: Return to the earliest failing oracle, structure or browser stage and invalidate dependent receipts.

iteration_budget.review_trigger: any clipped toolbar, lost workbench state, or fixed-browser regression

stop_conditions: failure baseline rejected and current browser accepted
source, accessibility, keyboard, responsive and visual gates pass
project and user-root references are updated and validated
the exact release artifact passes download verification

promotion_decision.reason: Global-container versus owner-local peer navigation recurs across operator consoles.

writeback: Project geometry and screenshots stay in LocalFlow evidence; the reusable ownership rule and negative fixture live in the user-root operator interaction catalog.
